newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks seen volatile on options expiry.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks seen volatile on options expiry.

text.p: Brazil shares are seen set for another volatile session Monday, with speculative trades setting the tone of the market ahead of Monday's options settlement, brokers said.

Investor attention is likely to focus on Telebras options at strike price of 150 reais as the company's preferred share, which is the underlying stock for the most active options, ended the week at 150.10 reais in the spot market.
On Friday, shares closed slightly lower, with investors jostling for position ahead of today's options expiry.
"The battle (between options holders) is likely to continue this morning," said private bank Bozano, Simonsen in its daily report.
Despite Monday's expected volatility, traders said the bolsa's uptrend remains mainly because of strong capital flows.

Market turnover has been increasing significantly in recent sessions, reaching over $1.0 billion a day, boosted by local and foreign buy orders. Domestic equity funds in particular have been a steady player in the market, purchasing not only blue-chips but also second-tier stocks, traders said.

Analysts said they would also keep an eye on steel stocks which on Friday dropped sharply on reports the government had begun a probe into allegations of price-fixing and excessive price increases in the steel, aluminum and pharmaceutical sectors.
